decisions.evidence: Round 1 maker: “Add ... bookmarks via a modal dialog” and “URL ... per bookmark”; validation “rejects empty/invalid URLs.” Round 1 client: “sufficient for saving ... my bookmarks.”
decisions.note: The presented URL-based save behavior conforms. Implementation-review stage.

decisions.evidence: Round 1 maker: “Add / edit ... bookmarks via a modal dialog” with “title, description ... per bookmark.” Round 1 client approves the application as it stands.
decisions.note: The add and edit dialogs provide title/description editing before and after saving. Implementation-review stage.

decisions.evidence: Round 1 maker presents editing with the field inventory “URL, title, description, and tags per bookmark,” omitting bookmark notes. Round 1 client only says the app is “sufficient” for editing and is “happy ... as it stands.”
decisions.note: The presented editable fields omit the required note field. The client's broad approval neither identifies nor explicitly accepts that difference. Implementation-review stage.

decisions.evidence: Round 1 maker: “Add / edit / delete bookmarks via a modal dialog” and verified API “delete” endpoint. Round 1 client approves the application.
decisions.note: Bookmark deletion is presented as supported. Implementation-review stage.

decisions.evidence: Round 1 maker says titles merely “default to the site host if left blank,” while “Favicons [are] fetched per site,” and offers “auto-fetching page titles” as a possible next step. Round 1 client says only that the current application is sufficient and satisfactory.
decisions.note: The future-step wording establishes that automatic target-page title collection is absent, so the required automatic metadata collection diverges even though favicon fetching exists. The client does not state this expectation or difference. Implementation-review stage.

decisions.evidence: Round 1 maker calls the UI “clean” and reports that it “renders the seed cards and tag chips,” while separately listing bookmark fields and favicon fetching. Round 1 client gives general approval but does not describe the list contents.
decisions.note: The record establishes a card list but does not clearly establish whether every item exposes title, description, tags, and favicon as required; the client's approval does not resolve that evidentiary ambiguity. Implementation-review stage.

decisions.evidence: Round 1 maker: “URL, title, description, and tags per bookmark” and “tags are deduplicated and lowercased.” Round 1 client calls the app sufficient for organizing bookmarks.
decisions.note: The presented bookmark form supports assigning tags, including multiple deduplicated tags. Implementation-review stage.

decisions.evidence: Round 1 maker: “Tag sidebar with per-tag counts; click a tag to filter, click ‘All’ to clear.” Round 1 client approves the application.
decisions.note: Selecting a tag to filter its bookmarks conforms directly. Implementation-review stage.

decisions.evidence: Round 1 maker scopes “Full-text search across title, description, URL, and tags,” omitting note content. Round 1 client says it is sufficient for “finding” bookmarks but does not mention the missing note-search expectation.
decisions.note: The explicitly presented search-field scope omits required bookmark notes. General satisfaction is not explicit recognition or acceptance of the difference. Implementation-review stage.

decisions.evidence: Round 1 maker offers “importing browser bookmark exports” only as a direction the app “could ... take ... next.” Round 1 client responds that the application is sufficient “as it stands,” without mentioning import.
decisions.note: Import is explicitly presented as not yet implemented. The client neither requests it nor states awareness and acceptance of its absence, so the divergence passes unexpressed. Implementation-review stage.
